memory_update.text: SEI should be tracked as a signed-contract, mid-cap AI data-center firm-power candidate with direct >500 MW and >600 MW contract disclosures; key risks are execution, financing, fuel-risk allocation, and counterparty concentration.

WLDN is a low-attention services candidate for data-center utility interconnection, energy optimization, and AI-related substation construction-management work; materiality of AI/data-center revenue remains a coverage gap.

For AI data centers, the underfollowed bottleneck appears to be shifting from generic utility ownership to project execution: firm MW contracting, temporary/on-site generation, interconnection engineering, substation construction, transmission upgrades, and fuel-chain security for advanced nuclear.

node: Firm power, nuclear fuel chain, grid interconnection, and data-center energy project execution
summary: Expanded the universe around AI data-center power constraints with a deliberate underfollowed lane. The strongest small/mid-cap discovery candidates found in this pass are not hyperscalers or large utilities; they sit in temporary/on-site generation, utility/data-center engineering, electrical construction, and nuclear fuel. The common chokepoint is not just electricity supply, but the ability to secure firm megawatts, interconnect facilities, build substations/transmission, and eventually fuel advanced nuclear capacity. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
